subject: Geo outage: temporary tenant steering guidance and verification checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-corp.com, maria.garcia@finserve.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-12-03T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Geo outage: temporary tenant steering guidance and verification checklist

Hi all,

Quick update and immediate mitigation guidance following the partial outage affecting our US-EAST and EU-WEST serving clusters that started ~07:50 PST this morning. We’ve opened RED-1345 and are working the root cause with the cloud provider; primary impact is increased latency and periodic 5xxs for tenants routed to the affected POPs.

What we’re asking customers to do now (prioritized, minimal changes):
1) Prefer regional fallback host — set your API host header to the nearest unaffected region for critical traffic. Use: us-west-1.primary.redwood.ai (US fallback) or eu-central-1.primary.redwood.ai (EU fallback). This avoids upstream peering paths into the degraded zones.
2) Reduce DNS TTL to 60s (if you control DNS) for the next 6 hours to accelerate baked-in failovers.
3) If you use our region selector header, set X-Redwood-Region to the fallback region (example: X-Redwood-Region: us-west-1).
4) If you have a proxy or VPC connector, prefer the alternate egress path documented in the attached tenant-steering-checklist.csv.

We are providing the traffic-shift-runbook.pdf (attached) which contains step-by-step commands and verification probes. Ben and Neha are on SRE rotation for live verification; Laura is tracking customer comms and will publish a short status update for your stakeholders.

Expected window for drift: ~2–4 hours to stabilize after changes. Please reply with the customer-facing contact you want us to coordinate with directly and whether you want Redwood to apply temporary routing on your behalf (we can do this for customers with delegated routing configured).

Attachments: tenant-steering-checklist.csv (small CSV checklist), traffic-shift-runbook.pdf (runbook snippets + curl checks)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — we see elevated error rates from our production tenants that correlate with the time you noted. A couple quick questions before we proceed:

- Do you recommend making a DNS change (CNAME) or relying on the X-Redwood-Region header for a faster flip?
- If we do DNS, will there be any cert rotation or SNI implications for our clients?

We’re happy to accept Redwood applying the routing change on our behalf if it’s faster — please confirm what scoped permissions you need. We’d like to plan for a 30-minute verification window and will only shift in batches (pilot 10% traffic).

— Acme Platform Ops (oncall)

On Mon, Dec 3, 2028 at 09:02 AM Acme Platform Ops <ops@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — we see elevated error rates ... Do you recommend making a DNS change or relying on the X-Redwood-Region header?

Short answer: both work but header-based routing is the fastest and has zero cert/SNI impact. If you control DNS and want a full tenant-level shift, reduce TTL to 60s and update the CNAME target to us-west-1.primary.redwood.ai; no cert rotation required — we serve the same SANs.

If you prefer Redwood to perform the change we need:
- Delegated routing token (one-time, can be revoked) OR
- A signed ticket (we’ll provide the exact CNAME) and your ops authorizer on call.

Pilot plan (recommended):
- Pilot: 10% traffic -> verify 5xx rate and p95 latency over 15 minutes
- Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% every 15 minutes if stable

We’ll run active health checks and provide a live dashboard link; Neha will post verification when p95 latency and 5xxs are within baseline. I’ll start the pilot if you give the go.

— Ben Carter
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident: Geo impact summary, actions taken, and verification (RED-1345)

Hello — final update and verification checklist now that services have been stable for >12 hours after mitigation. Thank you for working with the SRE squad on the pilot traffic shifts. Below is a concise post-incident summary and actions for your records.

Incident summary:
- Start: 2028-12-03 07:50 PST. Intermittent 5xx and elevated p95 latencies observed for tenants routed to US-EAST and EU-WEST due to a provider peering degradation.
- Impact: Affected ~8% of customer traffic across the impacted POPs; intermittent request failures and latency spikes up to 3–5x baseline for impacted flows.
- Mitigation: On 2028-12-03 09:35 PST we initiated tenant steering to fallback regions (us-west-1, eu-central-1) using header routing and DNS changes for delegated customers. Pilot -> ramp -> full for opt-in tenants.

Actions taken by Redwood:
- Executed pilot traffic shift for five delegated tenants (10% -> 100%) per agreed ramp plan.
- Performed continuous health checks and rolled back for any tenant exceeding the 5xx threshold.
- Requested and verified TTL adjustments where customers had DNS control.
- Engaged cloud provider; provider confirmed fix at 2028-12-03 15:50 PST and we started rehoming traffic back to normal routes.

Customer-facing validation checklist (please confirm the items below):
- [ ] You observed reduced p95 latency to baseline within the verification window.
- [ ] 5xx rates returned to pre-incident norms.
- [ ] Any delegated routing tokens used have been rotated (if applicable).
- [ ] Confirm whether you want Redwood to revert DNS/CNAME changes on your behalf or prefer manual revert.

Deliverables attached/linked:
- Attached: tenant-steering-checklist.csv, traffic-shift-runbook.pdf
- Postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/pm/20281203-geo-outage-summary (comments welcome)
- Jira: RED-1345 (root cause + mitigation tasks)

Next steps (for ops):
- Please complete the validation checklist and reply to this thread. We will mark the incident as mitigated in your tenant record once verification is confirmed.
- If you need Redwood to perform the revert, reply with the authorization method (delegated token OR signed ticket) and target revert window.

Thanks again for the fast collaboration. We’ll post the finalized postmortem and action items in the drive link above and follow up with a scheduled review if you’d like one.

Regards,
